title: Revert detection in gap-to-feature.ts only recognises gits DEFAULT revert message format, and a conventional-commits rev
description: Revert detection in gap-to-feature.ts only recognises gits DEFAULT revert message format, and a conventional-commits revert silently inverts its own meaning. Two independent checks both miss it. (1) landedCommitVerdict skips a gap-matching commit only when its subject matches /^Revert[\s"]/i — a subject of the form revert(scope): ... does not match, because a parenthesis follows Revert rather than whitespace or a quote. (2) shaWasRevertedInAnyClone greps for the pattern reverts (commit )?<sha>, so any words between reverts and commit defeat it; the prose Reverts substrate-authored commit dbb2917 does not match. Measured live 2026-08-23: I reverted the inert landing dbb2917 with subject revert(rhythm-conductor-tick): undo dbb2917 and body Reverts substrate-authored commit dbb2917. Both detectors missed it, so the revert was counted as a SECOND matching landing for route-edit-56849210 rather than as a revert. Since landedCommitVerdict returns present at two or more non-reverted landings and present closes the gap as already_resolved, the effect of reverting was to move the gap TOWARD a false close — the exact outcome the pending guard exists to prevent. Re-amending the commit to gits default subject Revert "<original subject>" plus the trailer This reverts commit <full sha>. made both detectors fire and dropped the count to zero. The existing code comment at shaWasRevertedInAnyClone already records that an operator rewriting a revert message defeated a trailer-only grep once before; this is the same class one level up, now in the subject test as well. Fix: accept the conventional-commits revert forms revert(scope): and revert: in the subject test, and loosen the prose pattern to allow words between reverts and the sha. Edit site repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/gap-to-feature.ts.
